newsitem.title: POLAND: France's Chirac visits Auschwitz, urges vigilance.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac visits Auschwitz, urges vigilance.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, visiting the former Nazi extermination camp at Auschwitz on Friday, called for vigilance against possible future anti-Semitism.

Winding up a three-day visit to Poland, Chirac toured the Auschwitz-Birkenau complex in southern Poland where World War Two Nazi German invaders killed up to 1.5 million people, most of them Jews brought there from across Europe including France.

In a memorial book at the camp, Chirac wrote a quotation from philosopher Vladimir Jankelevitch saying that the countless deaths concerned everyone. Ceasing to remember this would complete the extermination.
"Let Auschwitz, a place of suffering and memory, make us vigilant," Chirac added.

At a ceremony in France last year commemorating a 1942 roundup of Paris Jews by the collaborationist Vichy regime's police, Chirac recognised that the French state shared responsibility for deporting Jews to Nazi camps during the war.
At the time, Chirac, in a clear warning against the extreme-right National Front, also urged vigilance against attempts by some political parties to promote racist and anti-Semitic ideology.
On Friday Chirac, accompanied by his Polish counterpart Aleksander Kwasniewski, laid a wreath and joined in a minute's silence at the Auschwitz camp.
Then he went on to the larger Birkenau site, where in the company of French and Polish school students, he laid flowers at an international memorial to the victims of fascism.
